content.title: About
content.content: The falafel sandwich is a nutritious vegetarian sandwich featuring a spiced chickpea patty placed between slices of bread or wrapped in a flatbread together with vegetables, sauces, and herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Falafel originated in the Middle East and is a staple in Mediterranean cuisines.
The chickpea patty is rich in plant protein and often used as a meat alternative.
There are many serving styles: in pita, in a wrap, on a bun, or as a standalone burger.
Traditionally falafel is deep‑fried, but it can also be baked for a lighter version.
In some regions beans are used instead of chickpeas in the mixture.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas, the main ingredient, provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Falafel contains folate, thiamine, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals support blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When baked, falafel remains a low‑saturated‑fat option.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: High calories when fried
items.content: Traditional deep‑fried falafel can be calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Chickpeas contain oxalates, which in excess may contribute to kidney stone formation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the falafel sandwich hot, adding fresh veggies (tomato, cucumber, lettuce), sauces (tahini, yogurt, hummus), and aromatic herbs. It can be eaten by hand or with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Falafel patties can be frozen for up to 3 months; reheat before serving in an oven or microwave.
